SMTO-LLM-0072 — The model server's log isn't available in SMTO

GUID: a6d681af-6c52-5e7e-98ca-2db3353ef893
Slug: local-ai-log-unavailable
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: local_ai

What happened

  • SMTO still knows about this model server, but it doesn't have its log. SMTO keeps logs only while the Gateway that started the server keeps running, so a log may still exist on that computer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who manages the Gateway computer to look at the model server's own log on that computer. SMTO lost its copy of the log when the Gateway restarted, but the model server program may keep its own.
  2. If you need SMTO to show logs from now on, ask SMTO to start a new model server from your profile once the old one is confirmed stopped. SMTO keeps a log for any model server it starts, for as long as that Gateway keeps running.

What success looks like

  • You can read the log on the Gateway computer, or SMTO shows the log for a model server it started.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Note that SMTO can't rebuild the missing log, so don't wait for it to reappear.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Local AI runtime record has no in-memory log buffer on this Gateway, typically because it was restored after a Gateway restart or never got a live process handle.

What this means

  • The runtime record lacks the current owner's in-memory log buffer, commonly after ownership restoration without a live process handle. Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.

Why this can happen

  • The runtime record lacks the current owner's in-memory log buffer, commonly after ownership restoration without a live process handle.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare runtime ownership and Gateway lifetime with the original start receipt; check the provider's own authorized logging separately.

How to fix it

  • Log buffers are memory-only and are not saved in runtimes.json, so a runtime restored after Gateway replacement (or one whose launch failed) has none. Read the provider's own logs on the Gateway host (service manager or the provider's log location); a newly started SMTO-managed runtime will expose logs via local_ai.logs.
  • Use the provider/operator's retained logs when available, or preserve the missing-log limitation when investigating the original runtime.

Retry and execution caution

  • Only after exact state reconciliation.

How to verify the fix

  • A current owned runtime exposes its bounded log buffer; an old missing buffer is recorded as unavailable rather than reconstructed.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations or stop externally owned processes.

Technical notes

  • Local AI management belongs to the selected Gateway and accepted profile. Starting a runtime does not activate it for the controller; recorded execution and unknown-effect facts determine whether reconciliation is required.
